newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends down, soyoil up on commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends down, soyoil up on commercials.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mostly lower amid heavy fund selling while soyoil futures were higher, lifted by strong commercial buying amid talk China had purchased South American soyoil, traders said.
"There was Chinese talk in the soyoil market, 25,000 tonnes of Argentine oil bought overnight," said Jerry Gidel, analyst at Dean Witter.
The soyoil rumors were bolstered by aggressive commercial buying that wiped out heavy fund sales. Traders said funds sold at least 3,000 lots soyoil on the day and at least 1,000 lots soymeal.

Meal was also hit by the 135 lots of soymeal posted for delivery against the May contract on Wednesday. Traders pointed to the weak expiration of the May on Tuesday and reports of declining cash basis levels.
Cash brokers said soymeal basis levels fell by $1.00 per ton in Chicago and Danville, Ill., on Wednesday. The drop suggested that nearby demand was weakening, traders said.
Soymeal ended $2.40 per ton lower to $0.70 higher with July down $0.50 AT $284.80. Soyoil ended 0.26 to 0.21 cent per lb higher with July up 0.26 at 23.45.
Commercials were aggressive buyers of soyoil on the day, led by ADM with 1,200 lots of July. Cargill Inc bought at least 1,000 lots July and 100 August, pit sources said.
Funds were largely on the sell side. Smith Barney sold 1,200 lots July and 1,000 lots August while Prudential Securities sold 1,000 July.
In soymeal, FIMAT Futures sold 600 lots December, SAK sold 400 July and R.J. O'Brien sold 300 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 26,367 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 22,000 lots, against Tuesday's 23,593.
